summary: JIT credential orchestration gaps: GCP→AWS role chaining and network-tag authorization for LLM debug proxy
description: Issue summary: The ephemeral credential broker that bridges GCP Workload Identity Federation (WIF) to AWS STS for the dedicated LLM debug proxy is intermittently failing policy checks when network tag conditions are present on the target AWS role. Impact: Internal SRE/Platform engineers intermittently cannot assume the debug role in prod, causing inability to reproduce customer-facing Dedicated provisioning failures and blocking live debug sessions. Scope: observed in prod us-east for the dedicated control plane; affects debug/trace sessions for multiple LLM models. Hypothesis: a tag-based condition on the AWS role assume-policy combined with our broker's session tags causes role policy rejection when the broker attempts to pass truncated or non-canonical tag values. This is surfaced only when requests route through the LLM proxy because the proxy injects environment tags and request metadata before assume-role.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) From a GCP service account configured with WIF, call the internal LLM debug proxy with --debug-auth=jit flag. 2) Proxy attempts to exchange WIF token at the broker to assume an AWS diagnostic role with tag condition (e.g., 'x-org:session-owner=*'). 3) Observe STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity response. 4) Failure mode: AssumeRole denied with 'Condition check failed' and 'Tag value mismatch' logged in AWS CloudTrail. 5) Repeat without proxy injection of metadata (direct broker call) — often succeeds. This reproduces ~6/10 attempts in prod under current traffic patterns.
observed_behavior: STS assume-role calls intermittently denied. CloudTrail shows Condition statement failure referencing aws:TagKeys or aws:RequestTag. Broker logs show session-tags payload that include duplicated 'env' and 'request_id' keys; in some cases values are truncated to 32 characters. Proxy adds a 'proxy-origin' tag with URL-encoded path which causes the AWS policy string comparison to fail.
expected_behavior: Broker should reliably forward canonical session tags that match the AWS role's condition checks. LLM debug proxy should not mutate or truncate tag values in a way that violates assume-role policy conditions.
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Maya): reproduced locally with a minimal proxy + broker pairing; confirmed that proxy URL-encoding triggers percent-encoded values which our broker does not decode prior to calling STS. Diego: identified an edge case in internal tag dedupe logic — when the total tags payload > 8 entries, we compact tags and may truncate strings to 32 chars. Hypothesis chain: (1) Proxy injects encoded path; (2) broker dedupe/truncate code shortens value; (3) AWS role condition expects full canonical value; (4) policy denies. Observability gap: request-level tag snapshot not persisted in long-term traces. Temporary mitigation applied to increase broker debug logging for tag payloads. Also verified the role policy is strict by design due to compliance constraints (see linked confluence).
mitigation_workaround: 1) Short term: revert proxy metadata injection for debug sessions in prod by toggling feature flag 'proxy.inject_debug_meta' -> false. 2) Add temporary retry logic with backoff in the broker when AssumeRole returns Condition failure, coupled with expanded logging (already rolled out to 3% traffic). 3) For urgent ad-hoc debugging, SRE can create a time-limited AWS role without strict tag conditions and request ops to map it to the session (requires approval).
proposed_fix: 1) Update broker tag pipeline: ensure URL-decoding of proxy-injected metadata prior to dedupe; preserve full tag strings (remove 32-char truncation) and enforce canonicalization rules. 2) Add deterministic tag order and stable hashing to avoid duplicate keys. 3) Harden unit tests for tag serialization/size limits and add end-to-end test covering WIF→broker→STS with proxy injection. 4) Small IAM change: add a 'proxy-origin-normalized' attribute to role conditions and support both forms during phased rollout to avoid immediate access breakage. 5) Security review: require secops signoff for IAM condition change. Estimated engineering work: 3s — 1 week to implement + 2 days for rollout and verification.
rollout_plan: - Stage 1 (canary): deploy broker tag pipeline changes to staging and a 1% prod subset; monitor assume-role success rate and CloudWatch/CloudTrail errors for 48 hours. - Stage 2 (ramp): 10% for 24 hours, then 50% for 24 hours. - Stage 3: full rollout with IAM role conditional allowance for 'proxy-origin-normalized' for 24 hours; then remove temporary allowance after verification. - Rollback: revert broker change (toggle feature flag) and re-enable proxy injection if failures increase > 3x baseline in 15-minute windows. - Post-deploy: run conformance job that simulates 1k assume-role exchanges per minute for 30m and validate zero Condition failures.
approvals_needed: - Security: secops@redwood.ai signoff for any IAM condition change. - Compliance: verify that adding 'proxy-origin-normalized' does not open policy bypass vectors. - SRE: approval for toggling proxy injection flag in prod during mitigation. - Product/Privacy: confirm debug path metadata is acceptable to PII policy. Contact list: @Leah Singh (SecOps), @Omar Patel (Compliance), @SRE-Oncall.
follow_up_tasks: - Create automated trace snapshots for broker tag payloads (owner: Diego). - Add e2e test covering percent-encoded metadata (owner: infra-qa). - Update runbook for JIT broker failures (owner: Maya). - Schedule postmortem if incident recurs within 7 days after full rollout.
comments: Maya Chen (2026-03-10): Raised after customer-facing dedicated provisioning debugging blocked. Attached CloudTrail snippets and correlation IDs.
Diego Alvarez (2026-03-11): Confirmed reproduce locally; starting broker fix branch. Creating PR to decode/normalize tags before assume-role. Adding detailed unit tests.
Leah Singh - SecOps (2026-03-11): We need to ensure IAM change doesn't widen trust boundary. If feasible, prefer broker change only and avoid changing role conditions. I'll review PR when available.

SRE Oncall (2026-03-12): Toggled 'proxy.inject_debug_meta' flag to false for prod; observed immediate reduction in Condition failures. Rolling this flag change back will be part of staged rollout after broker fix.

Diego Alvarez (2026-03-12): PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4258 — patch decodes percent-encoded tag values and removes dangerous truncation. Requesting code review and secops triage.
